outcome: No result found since 26 January 2024 changes what a careful person would write in this bullet: the Zarankiewicz crossing-number conjecture for complete bipartite graphs remains open, with the same pre-2024 verified small cases (m ≤ 6, and K7,7, K7,8, K7,9) and the same pre-2024 lower bounds (Brosch–Polak's semidefinite-programming bound, arXiv:2206.02755 v2, October 2023; a flag-algebra bound giving cr(Kn,n) ≥ 0.9118·Z(n,n), September 2023).
summary: Searches for post-January-2024 activity on Turán's brick factory problem / the Zarankiewicz crossing-number conjecture (cr(K_{m,n}) = Z(m,n)) turned up no result that changes the bullet as stated. The live Wikipedia articles for both 'Turán's brick factory problem' and 'Zarankiewicz crossing number conjecture' still describe the conjecture as open, verified only for min(m,n) ≤ 6 and for K7,7, K7,8, K7,9 (Kleitman 1970, Woodall 1993), with the best lower bound still the pre-window 83%-of-Zarankiewicz-bound result. An AI-search summary tool asserted, without a traceable source, that K8,8/K8,9/K8,10 had also been verified; I could not substantiate this in either Wikipedia article or any paper found, so I treat it as a search-synthesis artifact rather than a fact, and it would predate 2024 in any case since it rests on the same Kleitman/Woodall parity argument. The one genuinely new, AI-adjacent 2026 item found — 'New Bounds for Zarankiewicz Numbers via Reinforced LLM Evolutionary Search' (arXiv:2605.01120, submitted 1 May 2026), which used an LLM-driven evolutionary search (OpenEvolve) to find new bipartite-graph constructions — is about a different problem that merely shares Zarankiewicz's name: the extremal Zarankiewicz number Z(m,n,s,t), the maximum edges in a bipartite graph avoiding K_{s,t} as a subgraph. That is not the crossing-number quantity Z(m,n) in this bullet's conjecture (cr(K_{m,n})); the two are unrelated except by naming coincidence, per §3.1's 'related problem, not this problem' rule (same trap as the disambiguation note in the triage's own scope logic). No arXiv listing, survey, or Terence Tao / graph-drawing blog post found in this window reports a new exact case, an improved bound on cr(K_{m,n}) itself, or any disproof. I therefore agree with the triage's 'none' verdict; my independent search additionally surfaced and ruled out the LLM/Zarankiewicz-number paper as a false positive, which the triage's narrower queries did not encounter.
competing_reading: If a reader conflates 'Zarankiewicz number' (extremal forbidden-subgraph problem) with 'Zarankiewicz's conjecture' (crossing number of K_{m,n}, i.e. this bullet), the arXiv:2605.01120 LLM-evolutionary-search paper could be mistaken for AI progress on this problem. It is not: the quantities, the theorems, and the entire mathematical content are unrelated aside from both being attributed to Kazimierz Zarankiewicz. I am confident in excluding it, but flag the naming collision explicitly since a shallower pass could code this problem as ai_role 'bound' in error.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or repository posting, dated after 26 January 2024, that either (a) verifies Zarankiewicz's formula for a new pair (m,n) beyond the existing small cases, (b) improves the constant in the lower bound cr(K_{m,n}) ≥ c·Z(m,n) beyond the pre-2024 flag-algebra/semidefinite-programming results, or (c) exhibits a drawing of some K_{m,n} with fewer crossings than Z(m,n), thereby refuting the conjecture.

dead_ends: A search-engine synthesized answer claimed K_{8,8}, K_{8,9}, K_{8,10} had been verified for Zarankiewicz's conjecture; neither Wikipedia article nor any paper found supports this, and it appears to be a fabricated/garbled summary rather than a real result — checked and rejected.

arXiv:2605.01120 ('New Bounds for Zarankiewicz Numbers via Reinforced LLM Evolutionary Search') looked promising as an AI result but on inspection addresses the unrelated extremal Zarankiewicz number Z(m,n,s,t) (forbidden K_{s,t} subgraph edge count), not the crossing number Z(m,n) of this bullet — ruled out as a related-problem, not a case, per §3.1.

arXiv:2407.21206 ('On the Uncrossed Number of Graphs') studies a distinct crossing-related invariant (the 'uncrossed number') for complete bipartite graphs, not the crossing number itself — checked, not applicable to this bullet.
